subject: UTC-anchor approach for tri-region technical deep dive
messages:
From: Amelia Carter <amelia@stellarsys.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Rios <carlos.rios@stellarsys.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Request: technical deep dive across regions

Hi Jordan & Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Stellar Systems is keen to move to a technical deep dive next week with our architect leads in Boston, Munich and Sydney. The challenge: we need an overlap window that actually works for all three teams, and our calendar coordinator pointed out DST quirks for some participants.

Quick context:
- Attendees: Amelia Carter (Infra lead, Boston), Carlos Rios (Platform architect, Munich), Mei Tanaka (Solutions architect, Sydney) — Mei is on APAC hours.
- Goal: walkthrough of model routing, KV cache behavior, and a short run-through of expected latency profiles with our expected sequences.
- Duration requested: 75 minutes (40 min demo + 25 min Q&A + 10 min buffer)

I've attached an availability spreadsheet from our architects (stellarsys_architects_availability.xlsx). Can you propose 2–3 concrete slots (with UTC times) and a fallback plan in case DST differences shift during the rollout?

We prefer an approach that avoids forcing someone into late-night sessions if possible. If a single overlap isn't feasible, we can split into two shorter sessions (US/EU + APAC across a followup) but we'd like Redwood's recommendation.

Thanks — looking forward to options.

Best,
Amelia
Amelia Carter
Infrastructure Lead, Stellar Systems

Subject: Re: Request: technical deep dive across regions

Hi Amelia — thanks for the availability file. Looping in Grace (SE) and Stephanie (solutions scheduling).

Short answer: a UTC-anchor approach gives the cleanest mapping across DST transitions and reduces ambiguity in calendar invites. A few concrete proposals (all times in UTC, each 75 minutes):

- Option A: 2026-12-15 15:00–16:15 UTC (US morning / EU afternoon / APAC late evening)
- Option B: 2026-12-16 07:00–08:15 UTC (US very early / EU morning / APAC afternoon)
- Option C: 2026-12-17 12:00–13:15 UTC (middle-ground; splits burden but still within working hours for EU and APAC)

Attachments: I generated an overlap matrix with a UTC anchor view (utc_anchor_slot_matrix.csv) and an example .ics for Option A (proposed_session_invite.ics).

A couple of operational notes:
- We'll include a short pre-read and a 10-minute pre-call for environment checks (model artifacts, tokenized examples) to avoid hitting cold starts during the run.
- If Option A pushes APAC late (post-2300 local for Sydney), Grace suggests we either shift to Option B or run a split-delivery: core demo for US/EU then a condensed repeat for APAC.

Grace — can you confirm SE availability for the candidate slots and whether we should plan a split?

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: utc_anchor_slot_matrix.csv (CSV, 4KB)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Amelia Carter <amelia@stellarsys.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T11:20:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Request: technical deep dive across regions

Thanks Jordan. Confirming I'm available for all three proposed UTC slots — I can run either the single 75-min session or the split approach. A few practical recommendations from the SE side:

- Anchor to UTC in all calendar invites and include local time conversions in the description ("15:00 UTC = 10:00 EST / 16:00 CET / 02:00 AEDT"). This avoids DST ambiguity when calendars auto-convert.
- Don't assume identical DST rules: EU and US swap dates can cause a 1-hour shift for part of a week — using UTC avoids on-the-day surprises.
- For demos that run past local 22:00 in APAC, request that the Sydney architect join from a private office or allow them to call in; we can record the session but mark parts that might be sensitive.
- If we do two sessions, keep the second one to 45 minutes (demo highlights + Q&A).

Operational checklist (I'll own):
- SE pre-check (30 min) one business day prior
- Short runbook for attendees in invite (links to test data, expected tokens, and a fallback contact)
- Recording policy and whether Stellar wants a redacted recording

If Amelia confirms a preferred option, Stephanie can send the calendar invite using the UTC-anchor text and including the pre-read link.

Grace O'Connor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — Jordan and Grace, this is helpful. Quick responses:

- Preferred slot: Option A (2026-12-15 15:00–16:15 UTC) if APAC can tolerate a late join. Mei in Sydney pinged me and said she can stay until 02:30 local for this one, so Option A works.
- Recording: yes please record; we'll want a redacted copy for internal review.
- Pre-read: I'm uploading a short doc with our target sequences and a small test dataset to the Drive link you shared.

One ask: because Stellar will be doing procurement planning this quarter, can we include a 5-minute segment at the end on expected per-token economics at different batching/quantization configurations? Our procurement lead wants a quick cost expectation so we can budget.

If you can confirm SE availability, we'll lock Option A.

Best,
Amelia
